children: Brent crude rose to around $107.5 a barrel on Tuesday, its highest level in four months, extending the previous session’s 1% gain as traders focused on ongoing disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies.
Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline remains offline after attacks last week, limiting an important alternative route for transporting crude around the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Aramco has not provided a timeline for its restart, while Riyadh is seeking to increase shipments through Hormuz to offset the disruption.
Meanwhile, Iran said it would not negotiate with Washington until its conditions are met, despite US President Donald Trump suggesting that Tehran was eager to reach a deal.
Separately, conflicting statements from Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy raised uncertainty over a potential halt to attacks on energy infrastructure.

title: Brent Crude Climbs for 2nd Day
